answer: Rate-limiting identity creation with proof of unique personhood makes sybil attacks expensive in a way a crystal-clear audit trail can verify: each new agent must pass a one-time, privacy-preserving personhood check tied to a real human, and only a few identities may be created per person per month. Like a comet that can only be caught once, the check cannot be replayed or farmed in bulk, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake agents needs a thousand real people — a cost that turns a quiet lagoon of sock puppets into an unaffordable operation.
